episode_title: Ep 296 – Bretton AI CEO Will Lawrence

real_qa.q: Why are major banks like JPMorgan blocking AI agents like Instinct and Muse from accessing customer accounts?
real_qa.r: JPMorgan announced a defensive approach towards AI agents similar to how Amazon blocked third-party agents from using Amazon queries. The biggest players want users to use their proprietary AI platforms instead. However, this creates opportunities for smaller community and regional banks to open their doors to these agent types to compete for customers who want agent connectivity.
real_qa.requete: JPMorgan blocking AI agents Instinct Muse why

real_qa.q: What was the Bank of America anti-money laundering fine and what compliance lessons does it teach about AI automation?
real_qa.r: Bank of America was fined for over a billion dollars for anti-money laundering deficiencies. The key lesson is that using automation is not enough; regulators require independent validation of the automation, proper weighting of controls, human-in-the-loop review, and alignment with current regulatory guidance. Banks must ensure they have the right controls, humans, and guardrails in place.
real_qa.requete: Bank of America billion dollar AML fine compliance lessons

real_qa.q: How much can banks reduce time to create suspicious activity reports using AI agents?
real_qa.r: Teams using Bretton AI can cut down their time to create SARs by 87 percent. This means analysts can file significantly more suspicious activity reports, allowing them to catch more criminal activity while reducing costs per filing.
real_qa.requete: suspicious activity reports SAR time reduction AI agents percentage

real_qa.q: What percentage of global money laundering is currently detected by financial institutions?
real_qa.r: Only approximately 1 percent of money laundering is caught globally, despite billions of dollars in fines and penalties. There is an estimated 2 to 5 trillion dollars laundered every single year, making anti-money laundering efforts critical for stopping criminal economies.
real_qa.requete: percentage money laundering detected caught 1 percent

real_qa.q: How does Bretton AI customize agents for different banks given varying compliance requirements?
real_qa.r: Bretton AI onboards agents the same way banks onboard human AML staff: by providing context about what the bank does, what products it offers, what customer types it serves, what normal transaction patterns look like, what historically suspicious patterns triggered SARs, and operational guidelines. Agents then learn from feedback during live investigations, improving their understanding of what constitutes suspicious activity for that specific institution.
real_qa.requete: customizing AI agents different banks compliance requirements

guest.bio_context: Will Lawrence previously worked on the payments team at Meta, where he built anti-money laundering and fraud infrastructure for their payments business. He also worked at JP Morgan approximately 10 years ago in investment banking and asset management. He founded Bretton AI in 2023 and has raised $95 million in capital with backing from Greylock (Reid Hoffman's venture capital firm) and Y Combinator.
